title: Horizon dips measured from airliner windows with an iPhone theodolite app (earthlyskeptic, two flights, September 2025): heights from the flights' ADS-B track logs, the air of the day, and the radius they give

radius_enters_via.how: the heights come from the transponders' pressure altitudes placed in the GFS model's air (geopotential heights), the terrain at the horizon is found along the heading on a 6,371 km sphere, and the accelerations come from ADS-B ground speeds (GNSS)

verdict_rule: Dips that stay near zero at every height, or that grow linearly with height (a far edge at a fixed distance), would favour the plane; dips growing as the square root of the height above the horizon terrain, with one radius for all, favour the globe.

units.tilt: degrees, added to a reading to remove the aircraft's acceleration
